title: Add the auditor role, judged against BRIEF.md and owner goals
summary: Add an auditor role modelled on the existing audience role: a fixed recorded definition, a typed output, a core module that runs it, and an `athena audit` CLI command. It judges real outcomes against BRIEF.md and the owner's goals, not a job's own criteria. The warden is excluded. The audience is the owner, who wants a grader whose yardstick jobs cannot change.

defaults_applied.how: All code and tests are Rust.
New module tests; cargo test and clippy pass.
Auditor only; the warden is left out.
Criteria run the auditor through the fake driver.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands to run.
Protection is marked prose-only until the warden lands.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The audience role is the template: Role::Audience, AUDIENCE_PROMPT, core/src/audience.rs, tests/audience.rs, and the `athena audience` command.
The auditor is run on request through a CLI command. Cadence-based scheduling is a field only.
Enforcing the protected prompt and checks is the warden's job and is deferred.
The auditor changes nothing and its highest rung is Implementation.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`. It passes, including new tests that run the auditor against a fake driver and check that it records a typed finding.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.

roles.rs defines an auditor role with a fixed prompt constant and a valid RoleDefinition. The prompt says to judge outcomes against BRIEF.md and the owner's goals rather than a job's own criteria, to look at real outcomes rather than records, and to cite evidence for each finding.
Run `cargo test`. A test shows the auditor's brief contains BRIEF.md and not the job's acceptance criteria. Another shows a finding with no evidence is rejected.
Run `cargo run -- audit --help`, or the equivalent test. The command exists and, with the fake driver, produces a recorded auditor invocation visible to the owner in CLI output.
Role::Auditor has a name that round-trips through the parse and as_str functions in records.rs, and every exhaustive match on Role compiles.
No warden code is added. The change does not edit BRIEF.md, athena.toml, defaults.toml, or any workflow file. CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the auditor.

The change records that the auditor's prompt is protected from jobs only by being a fixed constant. The warden request will enforce protection. This is marked as prose-only in the docs or code comments.

out_of_scope: The warden role and its holds on landings
Changes to BRIEF.md, athena.toml or defaults.toml
departures: The previous attempt, which covered both roles, hit the 1800s deadline. Even the auditor alone touches many files, as the audience role did, so cost and time are above the reference.
